 # Changelog
 
+## 1.3.2 - Unreleased
+
+### Ledger Presentation
+
+- Failure logs show the exception, feature location and project frames before the full original backtrace. Credential redaction now matches the 2.x failure-log behavior.
+- Client-built Markdown escapes user markup; attachment captions show kind, size and available dimensions, unnamed files use step-derived names, and JSON previews are compact.
+- Hook item names are simplified without changing topology. Native global hooks remain Launch-scoped where observed; their independent Item-name checks are N/A, not fabricated hook items.
+- Preserve explicit native Before/After/AfterStep names through Cucumber's hook-created event, retaining retry labels and clearing scalar metadata on finalization.
+- Step-argument logs caption tables and DocStrings, align numeric columns without changing values, and omit the repeated step line. Argument-free steps have no description; Outline descriptions show Examples values on one line.
+- Assertion, failure-evidence and HTTP cards preserve diagnostic values, HTTP severity and existing sanitized bounds.
+- Keep structured HTTP and assertion bodies in their baseline format for native Cucumber and terminal formatters; apply Ledger cards only to the RP route.
+- Opt-in `RP_RUN_CONTEXT=true` adds allowlisted SDK, Cucumber, Ruby and CI metadata plus a default Launch description; explicit attributes and descriptions win. No workers attribute is generated on 1.x.
+- Opt-in `RP_PRESENTATION=rich` adds status pills, table-header accents and collapsible evidence to ReportPortal log messages only. Native Cucumber, terminal output, caller text and item metadata remain unchanged.
+- Preserve item hierarchy, identities, statuses, timestamps, ownership, log counts and attachment bytes. Presentation faults retain the original baseline with one warning; rich output preserves ERROR first lines and adds at most 1,024 bytes.
+- Released as a patch at the owner's request; the two opt-in switches are additive and off by default.
+
+### Fixes And Known Limitations
+
+- Fixed: Text attachments whose preview contained a NUL byte were rejected by ReportPortal and silently lost. Previews now escape NUL, so these attachments persist with unchanged bytes.
+- Known limitation: A native Cucumber log message containing a NUL byte is still not persisted on 1.x. SDK 2.x escapes it.
+
+### Verification
+
+- The local Ruby 3.1/3.3 x Cucumber 9/10 four-cell matrix is the accepted Ruby 3.1 and Cucumber 9 evidence (Decision 12); remote CI covers Ruby 3.3 with Cucumber 10. The final tested commit and results will be recorded after WP5 completes; no final verification is claimed yet.

# Changelog

## 1.3.2 - Unreleased

### Ledger Presentation

- Failure logs show the exception, feature location and project frames before the full original backtrace. Credential redaction now matches the 2.x failure-log behavior.
- Client-built Markdown escapes user markup; attachment captions show kind, size and available dimensions, unnamed files use step-derived names, and JSON previews are compact.
- Hook item names are simplified without changing topology. Native global hooks remain Launch-scoped where observed; their independent Item-name checks are N/A, not fabricated hook items.
- Preserve explicit native Before/After/AfterStep names through Cucumber's hook-created event, retaining retry labels and clearing scalar metadata on finalization.
- Step-argument logs caption tables and DocStrings, align numeric columns without changing values, and omit the repeated step line. Argument-free steps have no description; Outline descriptions show Examples values on one line.
- Assertion, failure-evidence and HTTP cards preserve diagnostic values, HTTP severity and existing sanitized bounds.
- Keep structured HTTP and assertion bodies in their baseline format for native Cucumber and terminal formatters; apply Ledger cards only to the RP route.
- Opt-in `RP_RUN_CONTEXT=true` adds allowlisted SDK, Cucumber, Ruby and CI metadata plus a default Launch description; explicit attributes and descriptions win. No workers attribute is generated on 1.x.
- Opt-in `RP_PRESENTATION=rich` adds status pills, table-header accents and collapsible evidence to ReportPortal log messages only. Native Cucumber, terminal output, caller text and item metadata remain unchanged.
- Preserve item hierarchy, identities, statuses, timestamps, ownership, log counts and attachment bytes. Presentation faults retain the original baseline with one warning; rich output preserves ERROR first lines and adds at most 1,024 bytes.
- Released as a patch at the owner's request; the two opt-in switches are additive and off by default.

### Fixes And Known Limitations

- Fixed: Text attachments whose preview contained a NUL byte were rejected by ReportPortal and silently lost. Previews now escape NUL, so these attachments persist with unchanged bytes.
- Known limitation: A native Cucumber log message containing a NUL byte is still not persisted on 1.x. SDK 2.x escapes it.

### Verification

- The local Ruby 3.1/3.3 x Cucumber 9/10 four-cell matrix is the accepted Ruby 3.1 and Cucumber 9 evidence (Decision 12); remote CI covers Ruby 3.3 with Cucumber 10. The final tested commit and results will be recorded after WP5 completes; no final verification is claimed yet.


## 1.3.1 - 2026-10-31

### Readable Logger And Runnable Examples

- Add local date/time with milliseconds and aligned severity to AppLog terminal summaries, retaining TTY colors and NO_COLOR behavior while removing the redundant APPLOG prefix.
- Keep native Cucumber and ReportPortal message bodies unchanged: report routing, JSON formatting and step ownership are unaffected by the terminal timestamp.
- Add terminal preview and nine-parameter Cucumber demos, including opt-in live RP delivery; retain compact summaries, explicit report:false precedence and secret-safe output.
- Align the independent installed-gem API/Playwright consumer with SDK 1.3.1 and the updated terminal assertions. Demo artifacts belong to the caller's working directory, not the installed gem directory.

### ReportPortal 26.0.7 Deployment

- Upgrade the companion Chart to 1.3.1 with ReportPortal 26.0.7 and locked official chart 26.10.26. Retain the upstream Kubernetes >=1.35 requirement; SDK and Chart release versions are 1.3.1.
- Add an isolated Docker Compose stack with the matching released service versions, successful migration/bucket initialization barriers, loopback-only routing, read-only video access and retention.
- Preserve anonymous GET/HEAD/Range video playback while checking denial of list/upload/delete and explicit read revocation. Document the pinned archived MinIO images and production mirror/scan requirement.
- Validate actual Helm and Compose backends, synchronous/asynchronous reporting semantics, native attachment bytes, UI statistics navigation and real Playwright recording playback.
- Fix the source live-regression task to bypass the default offline profile, and wait for the Typewords onboarding overlay without forcing UI clicks.
- Preserve the latest consumer guides. Distribute Gem and Chart archives, checksums and build provenance through GitHub v1.3.1; RubyGems publication, in-place historical-data migration and production HA certification remain separate operations.

## 1.3.0 - 2026-10-13

### Day-2 Security And Operations

- Release companion Helm Chart 1.3.0, retaining ReportPortal 26.0.5 and locked upstream chart 26.8.12; the chart and server versions are independent.
- Replace MinIO's unsafe anonymous `public` preset with object-read-only `s3:GetObject`. Preserve HEAD/Range video playback while denying anonymous listing, writes and deletes.
- Reconcile existing policies when `makePublic=false` or the video extension is disabled, without deleting recordings. Permission-inspection failures fail closed.
- Reconcile one stable 30-day current/noncurrent retention rule and a 4 GiB hard video quota on an explicitly configured 8 GiB MinIO volume. Document server-level incomplete-upload cleanup and physical-capacity monitoring separately.
- Use controller-neutral Prefix Ingress routes; validate a separate local Traefik deployment and document Huawei private-cloud controller, TLS, storage and backup prerequisites without claiming production certification.

### Regression And Distribution

- Preserve binary Multipart sources during metadata validation: older JSON parsers can retag their input as UTF-8, breaking non-ASCII log plus binary attachment requests on Ruby 3.3. Add a byte/encoding regression guard.
- Add opt-in, single-process duration and fault harnesses: an accepted 900-second run confirmed 811 logs, 750 seeded trade/margin pairs and CSV integrity; a separate real-RP proxy matrix passed 14 fault cases.
- Keep these repository QA harnesses and their mock dependencies outside the installed production gem. Preserve original evidence and documented retry ambiguity; this is not an exactly-once or zero-loss guarantee.
- Add validated GitHub CI and tag-driven release packaging for the gem, locked Helm chart and SHA-256 checksums. RubyGems.org/private-registry publication remains a separate operation.
- Apart from the version identifier and this Multipart compatibility fix, SDK runtime behavior is unchanged. Video recording stays caller-owned; anonymous video reads remain an intentional internal-network policy. No historical-report migration, Huawei live deployment, production HA or M5 certification is implied.

## 1.2.0 - 2026-10-12

### Reporting Experience

- Preserve severity across AppLog's terminal, native Cucumber and ReportPortal routes; support explicit report delivery and bounded, credential-redacted HTTP exchanges.
- Add structured assertion and caller-supplied failure evidence with explicit step/attempt ownership, without owning the browser or replacing the original failure.
- Parse Feature, Rule, Scenario, Background and Examples metadata, including localized keywords, Markdown DataTables and DocStrings.
- Add opt-in stable scenario identities, safe attribute mapping, and source/CI/TMS links while retaining the verified `SUITE -> STEP(hasStats=true) -> STEP(hasStats=false)` UI contract.

### Delivery And Safety

- Bound queued records, bytes and batches; expose completion barriers and receipts that distinguish business results from reporting completeness.
- Add durable spool transactions, artifact validation, quotas, checkpoints and controlled original-target replay, with documented ambiguity and duplication limits.
- Harden context ownership, capture closure, native BeforeAll/AfterAll observation, redaction, attachment collisions, TLS verification and sanitized video-upload degradation.
- Default to independent worker launches; use `RP_LAUNCH_UUID` for CI-owned shared-launch lifecycle rather than treating local file join as a distributed completion barrier.
- Constrain Cucumber to `>=9,<11` and cucumber-expressions to `>=17,<19`, preventing the observed Cucumber 10 native HTML/message incompatibility with expressions 19.

### Examples And Deployment

- Include an independent installed-gem API and Playwright 1.62 example with healthy and intentionally failing scenarios, native report inspection and optional live RP reporting.
- Validate the current runtime against ReportPortal 26.0.5; the companion Helm `1.2.0-rc.2` pins official chart 26.8.12 and includes isolated local/external-Secret deployment profiles and RabbitMQ vhost bootstrap correction.
- The Helm chart remains a deployment candidate. Its legacy public video policy permits anonymous writes/deletes and is not production-safe; the production fresh-install example disables that extension. Publishing the SDK does not certify that policy or an in-place database migration.

### Distribution

- Distribute the installable gem and companion chart through the GitHub `v1.2.0` release. RubyGems.org publication is a separate authenticated step, not implied by a GitHub release.
- No zero-loss/exactly-once, Cucumber 11, complete Ruby-version matrix, or production HA claim is made. Video recording/finalization stays in the caller's framework.

## 1.1.0

- Introduced Triple-Track Smart Logger, MinIO upload degradation and the 30-day video lifecycle initialization policy.

## 1.0.0

- Initial published gem with Cucumber reporting, BDD hierarchy alignment and the optional S3/MinIO Markdown video route.

# Configuration reference

Most projects start with only an endpoint, project, API key, and Launch name.
Keep defaults for batching, retry, identity, and video until a concrete need
appears. See [getting started](getting-started.md) for the first working run and
[advanced reporting](advanced-reporting.md) before tuning delivery behavior.

## Configuration files and profiles

The formatter loads configuration relative to the **process working directory**:

1. Built-in defaults.
2. YAML `default:` plus the selected YAML profile.
3. Environment variables, which override YAML values.

Programmatic `Config.load(overrides: ...)` applies explicit overrides last; normal
Cucumber consumers do not need it. Set `RP_CONFIG` to select a YAML path;
otherwise `.reportportal.yml` is searched before `config/reportportal.yml`.

Example **`.reportportal.yml` in your automation project root**:

```yaml
default:
  endpoint: https://reportportal.example.com
  project: clearing_tests
  launch: Ruby Cucumber
  launch_description: Synthetic clearing regression
  launch_attributes:
    - key: component
      value: clearing
    - value: smoke
  join: false

profiles:
  local:
    enabled: false
  ci:
    launch: Clearing CI
    require_complete_reporting: true
```

Inject `RP_API_KEY` externally; omit it from committed YAML. The configuration
file does not interpolate shell placeholders such as `${RP_API_KEY}`. A
top-level profile mapping (for example `ci:`) is also accepted, but using
`profiles:` keeps the intent clear. Canonical YAML keys are shown below; legacy
dotted `rp.*` names are normalized through the same environment-key map.

From **your automation project root**, after the [integration setup](getting-started.md#3-connect-reportportal-and-integrate-an-existing-project):

```sh
mkdir -p artifacts
CUCUMBER_PROFILE=ci RP_ENABLED=true bundle exec cucumber --profile rp
```

Expected: Cucumber uses the `rp` command profile from `cucumber.yml`; the SDK uses
the YAML `ci` profile. `CUCUMBER_PROFILE` explicitly selects the reporting profile.
When it is absent, the SDK infers a profile from Cucumber's `-p`/`--profile` argument.
Use the explicit environment variable when the two profile names differ.

## Connection and Launch

| Environment variable | YAML key | Default | Type / use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RP_ENABLED` | `enabled` | `true` | Boolean; `false` deliberately disables transport |
| `RP_ENDPOINT` | `endpoint` | Unset | RP base URL; do not append `/api/v1/<project>` |
| `RP_PROJECT` | `project` | Unset | RP project identifier |
| `RP_API_KEY` | `api_key` | Unset | Secret; required for enabled transport |
| `RP_LAUNCH` | `launch` | `Cucumber` | Launch display name |
| `RP_LAUNCH_UUID` | `launch_uuid` | Unset | UUID of an already-open, CI-owned Launch |
| `RP_LAUNCH_DESCRIPTION` | `launch_description` | Unset | Launch description |
| `RP_LAUNCH_MODE` | `launch_mode` | `DEFAULT` | RP Launch mode |
| `RP_ATTRIBUTES` | `launch_attributes` | `[]` | Environment: `build:42,smoke`; YAML: list of key/value or value-only objects |
| `RP_RERUN` | `rerun` | `false` | Boolean; request rerun Launch creation |
| `RP_RERUN_OF` | `rerun_of` | Unset | Original Launch reference for rerun |
| `RP_REPORTING_ASYNC` | `reporting_async` | `false` | Boolean; `true` selects `/api/v2` instead of synchronous `/api/v1` |
| `RP_CONFIG` | — | First existing default path | YAML file path, relative to the working directory unless absolute |
| `CUCUMBER_PROFILE` | — | Inferred from Cucumber CLI, otherwise none | Reporting YAML profile selector |

With `RP_ENABLED=true`, missing endpoint/project/key leaves transport inert and
the requested report incomplete (`metadata_failures=1`). No API/join/queue worker
is created. Set `RP_ENABLED=false` for local-only runs rather than relying on
missing credentials. A CI-owned UUID cannot be combined with `rerun`/`rerun_of`;
the conflict is rejected. See [shared Launches](ci.md#parallel-workers-and-a-shared-launch).

## Presentation and run context

Available in SDK 1.3.2; both additions are opt-in and off by default.

| Environment variable | YAML key | Default | Type / use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RP_PRESENTATION` | `presentation` | `plain` | Exact `plain` or `rich`; rich decorates client-built RP log cards only |
| `RP_RUN_CONTEXT` | `run_context` | `false` | Strict Boolean; add allowlisted Launch metadata and a default description |

An invalid `RP_PRESENTATION` value, including `fancy`, logs one constant warning
without echoing the value and falls back to plain. Invalid `RP_RUN_CONTEXT`
Boolean values are rejected; prefer explicit `true` / `false`.

```yaml
default:
  presentation: plain
  run_context: false
profiles:
  ledger:
    presentation: rich
    run_context: true
```

Rich mode never changes native Cucumber messages/HTML, terminal summaries,
arbitrary AppLog text, item names/descriptions, or Launch metadata. It preserves
every ERROR log's first line and adds at most 1,024 bytes per message; a budget
or first-line guard retains the plain card. A presentation exception instead
restores the original pre-Ledger baseline with one nonreflective warning.

Run context adds missing `sdk`, `cucumber`, `ruby`, `git.branch`, `git.sha` and
`ci.build` attributes. It reads only these environment sources, first non-empty
value from left to right:

| Attribute | Environment sources |
| --- | --- |
| `git.branch` | `GITHUB_REF_NAME`, `CI_COMMIT_REF_NAME`, `BRANCH_NAME` |
| `git.sha` | `RP_SOURCE_COMMIT`, `GITHUB_SHA`, `CI_COMMIT_SHA`; first 7 characters |
| `ci.build` | `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `CI_PIPELINE_ID`, `BUILD_NUMBER` |

Values are trimmed, capped at 128 characters, and omitted when empty. Explicit
attribute keys win; a non-empty explicit Launch description is retained.
Otherwise a one-line Cucumber/Ruby/branch description is generated.
The 1.x formatter never generates a `workers` attribute, even when `PARALLEL_TEST_GROUPS` is set.
No environment dump or implicit CI API lookup occurs. See
[Presentation](advanced-reporting.md#presentation) for the card and channel contract.

## Logger and reporting policy

| Environment variable | YAML key | Default | Type / use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RP_CONSOLE_MIRROR` | `console_mirror` | `false` | Boolean; mirror RP-only `rp_log` to STDOUT as `[RP-MIRROR]` |
| `RP_FAIL_ON_REPORTING_ERROR` | `fail_on_reporting_error` | `false` | Boolean; propagate synchronous reporting exceptions when no original business failure exists |
| `RP_REQUIRE_COMPLETE_REPORTING` | `require_complete_reporting` | `false` | Strict Boolean; require a complete final whole-run receipt after native execution/teardown |
| `RP_DEBUG_CURL_MODE` | `debug_curl_mode` | `false` | Boolean; emit transport replay diagnostics; evidence may be sensitive |
| `RP_DEBUG_CURL_DIR` | `debug_curl_dir` | `.reportportal-curl` | Directory for multipart replay data |

`RP_CONSOLE_MIRROR` does not add native HTML evidence or change AppLog routing.
AppLog's per-call `report:` choice is separate from configuration. Use
`NO_COLOR=1` for uncolored auto-selected AppLog output; it is not an RP YAML key.
The completeness policy differs from exception propagation: a background upload
failure can leave business execution successful while its receipt is incomplete.
See [CI reporting policies](ci.md#choose-the-reporting-policy).

## Batching, queue, and finalization

| Environment variable | YAML key | Default | Unit / use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RP_BATCH_SIZE_LOGS` | `batch_size_logs` | `20` | Positive record count per batch |
| `RP_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` | `batch_max_bytes` | `8388608` | Positive bytes; complete serialized HTTP batch body (8 MiB) |
| `RP_QUEUE_MAX_RECORDS` | `queue_max_records` | `1000` | Positive reserved-record count |
| `RP_QUEUE_MAX_BYTES` | `queue_max_bytes` | `16777216` | Positive accounted resident bytes (16 MiB) |
| `RP_QUEUE_OVERFLOW_POLICY` | `queue_overflow_policy` | `reject_new` | `reject_new` or `block` |
| `RP_QUEUE_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS` | `queue_admission_timeout_ms` | `100` | Positive milliseconds; bounded admission wait for `block` |
| `RP_FLUSH_INTERVAL` | `flush_interval` | `1.0` | Seconds; minimum normalized value `0.1` |
| `RP_EXIT_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS` | `exit_flush_timeout_ms` | `5000` | Milliseconds; one shared finalization budget |
| `RP_SPOOL_DIR` | `spool_dir` | `.reportportal-spool` | Private durable transaction directory |
| `RP_SPOOL_MAX_BYTES` | `spool_max_bytes` | `268435456` | Positive bytes; spool quota (256 MiB) |

Queue accounting includes a 256-byte metadata allowance per record. Overflow
can reject evidence; `block` is bounded waiting, not unlimited buffering.
An accepted queued record is not a server confirmation. Finalization's budget
is shared across closure, flushing, retries, item/Launch completion, and worker
join. Retain queued source files until finalization settles.

## ReportPortal HTTP transport

| Environment variable | YAML key | Default | Unit / use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RP_HTTP_OPEN_TIMEOUT` | `open_timeout` | `5` | Seconds, normalized to at least 1 |
| `RP_HTTP_READ_TIMEOUT` | `read_timeout` | `15` | Seconds, normalized to at least 1 |
| `RP_HTTP_WRITE_TIMEOUT` | `write_timeout` | `15` | Seconds, normalized to at least 1 |
| `RP_HTTP_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` | `retry_attempts` | `5` | Total attempt limit, including the initial attempt |
| `RP_HTTP_RETRY_BASE_INTERVAL` | `retry_base_interval` | `0.5` | Seconds; exponential-backoff base |
| `RP_HTTP_RETRY_MAX_INTERVAL` | `retry_max_interval` | `10.0` | Seconds; backoff cap |

These timeouts govern the SDK's RP HTTP client, not your test application's
HTTP client or browser. Configure those separately. A successful log response
after retry can still imply a duplicate from an earlier lost response; the
receipt records `possible_duplicates`.

## Scenario identity and business metadata

| Environment variable | YAML key | Default | Type / use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RP_IDENTITY_STRATEGY` | `identity_strategy` | `legacy` | `legacy` or explicit `stable_v1` migration |
| `RP_IDENTITY_ROOT` | `identity_root` | Working directory | Root for source-derived identity |
| `RP_IDENTITY_NAMESPACE` | `identity_namespace` | Unset | Keep fixed across workers sharing history |
| `RP_SCENARIO_ATTRIBUTES_ENABLED` | `scenario_attributes_enabled` | `false` | Boolean; allowlisted Scenario attributes |
| `RP_SCENARIO_ATTRIBUTE_KEYS` | `scenario_attribute_keys` | `component,team,owner,layer,priority,browser,tms` | Comma-separated allowlist, or YAML list |
| `RP_SCENARIO_ATTRIBUTES` | `scenario_attributes` | `[]` | Environment: JSON object/list; YAML: defaults for business attributes |
| `RP_SCENARIO_LINKS_ENABLED` | `scenario_links_enabled` | `false` | Boolean; description links, independent from attributes |
| `RP_SOURCE_URL_TEMPLATE` | `source_url_template` | Unset | Source URL template with `{commit}`, `{path}`, `{line}` |
| `RP_SOURCE_COMMIT` | `source_commit` | Unset | Full hexadecimal commit ID |
| `RP_SOURCE_ROOT` | `source_root` | Working directory | Root for source-link paths |
| `RP_CI_RUN_URL` | `ci_run_url` | Unset | Explicit complete CI run URL; no automatic provider detection |
| `RP_TMS_URL_TEMPLATE` | `tms_url_template` | Unset | TMS URL template with `{id}` |

`RP_TEST_CASE_ID` is read by the formatter as an explicit Scenario ID override;
it is not a `Config` YAML key. Otherwise ID tags such as `@tms:CASE-42` are used.
A process-wide override applies to every Scenario in that process, so prefer
per-Scenario tags for a suite containing distinct cases. Stable-v1 hashes an ID
seed into the wire `testCaseId`; it does not send the raw TMS ID as that field or
merge existing history. See [identity and metadata](advanced-reporting.md#scenario-identity-attributes-and-links).

## Legacy same-host join

| Environment variable | YAML key | Default | Unit / use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RP_CLIENT_JOIN` | `join` | `false` | Boolean; explicit legacy local-file coordination |
| `RP_CLIENT_JOIN_LOCK_FILE_NAME` | `join_lock_file_name` | `.reportportal.lock` | Lock filename |
| `RP_CLIENT_JOIN_SYNC_FILE_NAME` | `join_sync_file_name` | `.reportportal-launch.json` | Launch synchronization filename |
| `RP_CLIENT_JOIN_FILE_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` | `join_wait_timeout_ms` | `30000` | Milliseconds |

File join is deprecated for production shared completion. It is not a distributed
CI barrier: a primary can finish early, and late workers can split into another
Launch. `RP_LAUNCH_UUID` bypasses this local join and delegates the lifecycle to CI.

## Optional video / S3 storage

Ordinary image/JSON/text attachments need no MinIO configuration. Read
[video and storage boundaries](advanced-reporting.md#video-and-external-storage)
before using this optional route.

| Environment variable | YAML key | Default | Type / use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RP_VIDEO_UPLOAD_MODE` | `video_upload_mode` | `reportportal_multipart` | Default multipart; optional `minio_markdown` video route |
| `RP_MINIO_ENDPOINT` | `minio_endpoint` | `http://localhost:9000` | S3 upload endpoint; development default |
| `RP_MINIO_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | `minio_public_base_url` | `http://localhost:9000` | Browser-readable base URL; development default |
| `RP_MINIO_BUCKET` | `minio_bucket` | `automation-videos` | Dedicated video bucket |
| `RP_MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | `minio_access_key_id` | `minioadmin` | Development-only default; inject a real storage identity |
| `RP_MINIO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | `minio_secret_access_key` | `minioadmin` | Development-only default; inject secret externally |
| `RP_MINIO_REGION` | `minio_region` | `us-east-1` | S3 region |
| `RP_MINIO_SSL_VERIFY_PEER` | `minio_ssl_verify_peer` | `true` | Strict Boolean; verify the S3 HTTPS certificate |
| `RP_MINIO_SSL_CA_BUNDLE` | `minio_ssl_ca_bundle` | Unset | Readable trusted PEM CA-bundle path |

`RP_MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` is a compatibility alias for `minio_public_base_url`;
prefer `RP_MINIO_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` and avoid setting both. TLS options apply to the
optional storage uploader, not to the RP transport/browser or bucket access
policy. Use HTTPS, a trusted CA, explicit access controls, and retention settings
for real data; these development defaults are not production credentials.

## Validation and reference source

Use explicit `true`/`false` values for Booleans. Required-reporting and S3 peer
verification options reject invalid Boolean values rather than silently guessing.
Queue/batch/spool sizes and admission limits must be positive decimal integers.
Inspect configuration diagnostics by option name rather than printing secret
values. The [configuration implementation](https://github.com/NickYin0125/CucumberReportportal/blob/main/lib/reportportal_cucumber/config.rb)
is the source of these mappings/defaults.

# Advanced reporting Use this reference after [getting started](getting-started.md), [best practices](best-practices.md), and [CI setup](ci.md). It explains delivery contracts and optional capabilities; none of these settings is required for the minimal Scenario or ordinary PNG/JSON/text reporting. ## Presentation SDK 1.3.2 uses Ledger plain cards by default: project-first failures with complete backtraces, attachment metadata, compact JSON, argument captions, numeric table alignment, one-line Outline values, and assertion/HTTP/evidence cards. Numeric values, status levels, log counts, ownership, IDs and original attachment bytes are unchanged. Argument-free steps do not send descriptions. Enable the two independent options from your test project: ```sh RP_PRESENTATION=rich RP_RUN_CONTEXT=true bundle exec cucumber --profile rp ``` `RP_PRESENTATION` defaults to `plain`; invalid values warn once and use plain. `rich` accents **ReportPortal log messages only**, not native Cucumber HTML/messages, terminal summaries, caller AppLog text, names, descriptions or Launch metadata. It folds full backtraces, attachment previews over 20 lines, DocStrings over 20 lines, HTTP headers and HTTP bodies over 12 lines. Table headers are accented only for tables with at most six columns. Existing preview bounds still apply, with full original attachment bytes retained separately. Client-generated `
` is allowed in table cells; user markup is escaped. Every ERROR first line stays byte-identical. Added markup is limited to 1,024 bytes per message; exceeding that budget or changing an ERROR first line keeps the plain card. Helper exceptions retain the original baseline with one warning, not a partially formatted card. Rendering does not change Scenario outcomes. `RP_RUN_CONTEXT` defaults to `false`. When enabled it adds only the documented SDK/runtime/CI attributes and a one-line description if none was supplied; explicit values win. No `workers` attribute is generated on 1.x. See the [configuration allowlist](configuration.md#presentation-and-run-context). The owner-approved compatibility exceptions preserve baseline behavior: - Cucumber 9 rejects a single native step containing both a DocString and a DataTable. Its compound-syntax check is N/A with parser-failure evidence; separate argument steps still verify both presentations. Cucumber 12 retains native compound-argument coverage. - Native `BeforeAll` / `AfterAll` do not gain independent Hook Items. Existing Launch-scoped logs, exceptions and shutdown behavior remain unchanged; only their independent Item-name check is N/A. In 1.x, `BeforeAll` can run before formatter construction. Existing class-hook name mappings remain unit-tested. These are Decisions 4 and 5 in the [owner requirements](design/presentation-ledger-proposal.md#decisions), not waivers for ownership, failure propagation, or delivery checks. The opt-ins do not change ReportPortal viewer settings or introduce a new deployment requirement. ## Report structure | RP node | Wire type | `hasStats` | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Feature | `SUITE` | `true` | Business suite | | Scenario / executed Examples row | `STEP` | `true` | One statistical test | | Before / After Hook | `BEFORE_METHOD` / `AFTER_METHOD` | `false` | Hook evidence | | Given / When / Then | `STEP` | `false` | Action evidence | | `rp_step` manual group | `STEP` | `false` | Nested business action | Scenario is deliberately a statistical `STEP`, not `TEST`. The previously verified RP UI statistics drilldown selected statistical leaves with `type=STEP&hasStats=true&hasChildren=false`; nonstatistical children carry evidence without becoming additional tests. Background actions retain their `[Background]` prefix. Gherkin DataTables/DocStrings become Markdown descriptions and plain Step-argument logs (RP log accents are opt-in); every executed Examples row gets its own UUID. See the [metadata contract](design/reporting-experience-m3a-implementation.md). ## Launch ownership and native run hooks An ordinary process starts/finishes its own Launch. A worker supplied with `RP_LAUNCH_UUID` writes to an existing CI-owned Launch, bypasses local file join, and never starts/finishes that Launch. CI must collect every actual business exit and final reporting receipt, handle deadlines/crashes/late workers, and finish the shared Launch. See the [CI sequence](ci.md#parallel-workers-and-a-shared-launch). Legacy `RP_CLIENT_JOIN=true` remains a compatibility opt-in for same-host files, but is deprecated for production shared completion. Its primary can finish before secondaries; a later worker can split into another Launch after the primary exits. It is not a distributed barrier. Without an external UUID, the default `RP_CLIENT_JOIN=false` gives each worker an independent Launch. In native Cucumber 9/10, `BeforeAll` runs before formatter construction. If it aborts, the formatter creates no Launch and does not fabricate a class-hook item. A per-registry observer waits for genuine `AfterAll` before finalization. An `AfterAll` error becomes a credential-sanitized Launch-level ERROR log while its original exception retains precedence, including if reporting also fails. Native run hooks are not `BEFORE_CLASS`/`AFTER_CLASS` test-step nodes. This native observer uses Cucumber 9/10's private registry/configuration association; later major versions need separate compatibility work. A complete receipt never means the business run/teardown passed. Implementation and dated checks: [M4-B contract](design/reporting-experience-m4b-implementation.md), [M4-B verification](design/reporting-experience-m4b-verification.md). ## Bounded delivery and finalization RP calls go through `ReportportalCucumber::Http::Client`; optional S3 uploads use the AWS transport separately. Launch/item UUIDs are generated before creation and reused on retries, reducing creation-duplication risk. Retried logs can still duplicate when an earlier accepted response was lost. `Runtime::LogBuffer` delegates to a background `Service::QueueProcessor`. Defaults are 1,000 reserved records, 16 MiB accounted resident data (including 256 bytes metadata per record), 20 records per batch, and 8 MiB for the **complete serialized batch body**. Flushing occurs by count, bytes, or interval. Overflow rejects new records by default and is observable in diagnostics/receipts; `block` opts into a bounded admission wait (100 ms by default), not unlimited buffering. Path-backed attachments keep their paths for streaming. `StringIO` uses its full backing string without changing the cursor; arbitrary non-path IO is rejected without reading it. Text/JSON path previews use bounded reads. Native AppLog `file:` attachments still read the file into memory for Cucumber; choose `rp_attach(path)` for a large RP-only file. Keep source artifacts available until reporting settles. The default overload policy can lose evidence and is not a zero-loss guarantee. `sent_batches` counts successful local API calls, not server log receipts. Finalization shares one monotonic `RP_EXIT_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS` budget (default 5 seconds) across the barrier, transport retries, action/capture closure, item and Launch finishes, and worker join. It is not a fresh budget per item. A zero-timeout programmatic shutdown returns immediately without synchronously spooling outstanding work. See [configuration limits](configuration.md#batching-queue-and-finalization) and the [queue contract](design/reporting-experience-m4a-implementation.md). ## Delivery receipts and completeness The formatter's `reporting_receipt` returns an immutable `DeliveryReceipt`. Retain the reporter while Cucumber is active and inspect/export it after normal completion, as in the [CI receipt snippet](ci.md#retain-a-final-reporting-receipt). The formatter does not expose `flush`, `shutdown`, `flush_receipt`, or `shutdown_receipt`. On `Runtime::LogBuffer` / `Service::QueueProcessor`, Boolean `flush`/`shutdown` mean accepted work **locally settled** before return, not complete server delivery. Their receipt-returning `flush_receipt(timeout:)` / `shutdown_receipt(timeout:)` capture an accepted sequence cutoff; later producers do not extend it. | Field | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `cutoff` | Accepted sequence through which the barrier/snapshot is accounted | | `settled` | Records whose local processing settled | | `confirmed` | Synchronous v1 confirmations | | `accepted_awaiting_persistence` | v2 async acceptance; not confirmed persistence | | `spooled` | Retained local evidence, not completed server delivery | | `failed` | Failed records | | `ambiguous` | Server acceptance is unknown; a local spool copy may also exist | | `possible_duplicates` | A retry may have duplicated an earlier accepted attempt | | `pending` | Accepted records not yet settled | | `rejected` | Cumulative admission rejections; rejected records have no accepted sequence | | `capture_close_timeouts` | Actions/evidence capture that did not close in budget | | `metadata_failures` | Reporting configuration/start/finish failures | | `degraded_evidence` | Evidence degraded, for example external video reduced to plaintext | | `local_settled` | Local processing is settled, independently from confirmation | | `timed_out` | The relevant barrier/finalization budget expired | | `complete` | Whole reporting contract completed without unconfirmed/lost/degraded evidence or metadata failures | Counts describe delivery outcomes; do not add all columns to infer a total since ambiguity/duplication indicators can overlap other outcomes. Rejections are the cumulative count at a flush/shutdown cutoff and the whole-run total in the final formatter receipt. Counters/waiters are bounded; the receipt does not retain a run-long payload/outcome map. `complete=false` when accepted logs remain unconfirmed, an admission is rejected, capture fails to close, reporting start/finish fails, or video degrades. A successful log response after retry is marked `possible_duplicates`; even a confirmed retry does not justify claiming completeness if duplication is possible. `RP_REPORTING_ASYNC=true` selects `/api/v2`, whose acceptance is explicitly not synchronous persistence confirmation. `RP_FAIL_ON_REPORTING_ERROR=true` propagates synchronous reporting exceptions when no original business error exists; a log-only background failure can still leave a passing business exit with `complete=false`. For whole-report gating, use the separate `RP_REQUIRE_COMPLETE_REPORTING=true` policy described in [CI](ci.md#choose-the-reporting-policy). Requested reporting with missing endpoint, project, or key is inert but incomplete (`metadata_failures=1`); explicit `RP_ENABLED=false` bypasses that reporting requirement. ## Durable spool and controlled replay Exhausted/uncertain delivery can be retained as private, versioned spool transactions under `RP_SPOOL_DIR` (default `.reportportal-spool`), subject to the 256-MiB default quota. Existing unversioned NDJSON is inspectable but is not automatically imported/replayed. Spool is durable local evidence, not server confirmation; control access and retention as for other test artifacts. Replay is **transaction-scoped and dry-run by default**. It validates the selected transaction without credentials/network. Execution requires `--execute`, the same endpoint/project, and still-open original Launch/item targets. It cannot reopen/recreate targets. An interrupted `in_flight` record is uncertain; `--allow-duplicates` explicitly permits possible duplicate delivery for that transaction. Confirmed entries are never resent. Each entry has one replay HTTP attempt; a lost response remains ambiguous. Async v2 replay is refused. From **your automation project root**, with the installed SDK in its bundle, list committed transaction marker IDs without printing payloads: ```sh spool_dir="${RP_SPOOL_DIR:-.reportportal-spool}" for marker in "$spool_dir"/tx-*.ndjson; do [ -f "$marker" ] || continue printf '%s\n' "${marker##*/}" | sed 's/\.ndjson$//' done ``` Expected: zero or more `tx-...` candidate IDs. Candidate discovery is not validation; select one actual ID for dry-run. From **the same project root**: ```sh bundle exec reportportal-spool --spool-dir .reportportal-spool \ --transaction TRANSACTION_ID --dry-run ``` Expected: exit `0` for a valid inspection, with no HTTP requests. Replace `TRANSACTION_ID` with a listed ID. A valid dry-run can still describe unavailable artifacts: `unavailable_artifacts` is bounded to `0..1000`, and reasons are `[]` or `["source_unavailable"]`, including confirmed siblings. Such markers have no replacement source bytes. Recover originals separately; the SDK never fabricates them. A missing published blob/checksum mismatch is a hard error (exit `2`). When you have verified the open targets and matching configuration, with `RP_API_KEY` already injected, **from the same project root**: ```sh RP_ENDPOINT=https://reportportal.example.com RP_PROJECT=your_project \ bundle exec reportportal-spool --spool-dir .reportportal-spool \ --transaction TRANSACTION_ID --execute --timeout 30 ``` Expected: exit `0` only when requested confirmations were persisted; exit `2` when delivery remains refused/pending/failed/ambiguous. CLI syntax errors exit `1`. The timeout is seconds. Omit `--allow-duplicates` unless you deliberately accept the specific uncertainty; dry-run does not make a closed target replayable. Contracts: [persistence](design/reporting-experience-m4c-implementation.md), [replay](design/reporting-experience-m4c-replay-implementation.md). ## Failure evidence and action ownership Public World API: ```ruby rp_capture_target rp_evidence(action:, error:, url: nil, details: nil, artifacts: [], target: nil) ``` Capture the opaque target inside an open Gherkin Step/Hook/manual Step. It is nil when reporting is disabled/unavailable or no action is open. Passing it explicitly allows a helper to retain attribution while the original action remains open; join helpers before returning from that action. Execution context is isolated per runtime and thread/fiber. `Thread.current[:rp_context_stack]` and `Thread.current[:reportportal_cucumber_context_state]` are diagnostic, read-only snapshots of the most recently accessed context, not authoritative storage. Modifying them is unsupported and does not change evidence ownership. `rp_evidence` returns true when all admissions succeed; false covers unavailable reporting, invalid/foreign/closed targets, rejection, or cancellation. Admission is not server confirmation. Omitting `target:` chooses only the current open action. A late call never falls back to a Scenario, Launch, later Step, or Hook. An After screenshot must deliberately target its open After Hook. Each artifact accepts `path:` or `bytes:`, plus optional `name:` and `mime:`. Path-backed artifacts stream; in-memory bytes are limited to 1 MiB. A call accepts at most 16 artifacts; larger batches are rejected, not truncated. Admissions share one monotonic exit-timeout budget, and target closure cancels pending admission. Publication does not hold the context lock while waiting for queue space; closure/lock acquisition share finalization's budget. Some entries can already be accepted before a later one fails, so false is not rollback. Closure timeouts and rejections remain visible as incomplete reporting. See [UI recipes](best-practices.md#choose-step-evidence-or-after-hook-evidence) for Step/After capture, a single artifact route, and re-raising the original error. The [M2 evidence contract](design/reporting-experience-m2-implementation.md) documents implementation boundaries. ### Diagnostic privacy limits Failure/assertion diagnostic text is credential-redacted before clipping. Inputs over 64 KiB, malformed JSON-shaped diagnostics, and URLs that cannot be parsed safely are replaced with a fixed omission marker. The bounded policy also covers transport-error warning text and spool exception metadata. It does not sanitize raw files/video, ordinary AppLog text/JSON, low-level `rp_log`, automatic Step/manual-Step exception logs/backtraces, or native Cucumber failure payloads. A safe `rp_evidence` diagnostic followed by re-raising the original error can therefore still leave that error in separate failure channels. The sanitizer does not mutate or suppress original failures. Multipart transport preserves valid MIME/name associations and full attachment bytes, including collision-safe filenames for image, JSON, text, PDF, and binary files. Bounded previews are presentation aids, not a replacement for full evidence review or a universal privacy filter. ### RP-only World helpers Use these **inside Cucumber Steps/Hooks** when native HTML/messages are not required; use AppLog/native `log`/`attach` for both report tracks: ```ruby rp_log("Synthetic business checkpoint", level: :info) rp_log("Synthetic business checkpoint", "INFO") rp_attach("artifacts/failure.png", name: "failure.png", mime: "image/png") rp_attach(JSON.generate({status: "rejected"}), name: "response.json", mime: "application/json", message: "Sanitized response") rp_step("Prepare synthetic data") { rp_log("Data ready") } ``` `rp_log` supports keyword or positional levels and an `attachment:` Hash with `name`, `bytes`, and `mime`. Optional console mirroring requires `RP_CONSOLE_MIRROR=true`; `mirror: false` suppresses it for one call. `rp_attach` accepts `mime:` or its `mime_type:` alias. A String that names an existing file is treated as a path; otherwise it is treated as bytes. Retain path-backed files until delivery settles. These helpers do not add native evidence or assert a business outcome. ## Scenario identity, attributes, and links Identity remains `legacy` by default. To deliberately pilot stable identities, **from your automation project root**, with normal RP configuration injected: ```sh mkdir -p artifacts RP_IDENTITY_STRATEGY=stable_v1 RP_IDENTITY_ROOT="$PWD" \ RP_IDENTITY_NAMESPACE="clearing-ci" \ bundle exec cucumber --no-profile --publish-quiet --format progress \ --format ReportPortal::Cucumber::Formatter --out artifacts/reportportal.out ``` Expected: Scenario wire IDs use stable-v1 identity generation. Keep namespace/root policy consistent across workers sharing history. `RP_TEST_CASE_ID` (highest priority) or explicit tags such as `@tms:` seed opaque `rp:stable-v1:` `testCaseId` values; the raw seed is not the wire ID and raw-TMS UI search is not guaranteed. Migration starts a separate history baseline; it does not merge/rewrite/backfill server history. Review the [identity migration contract](design/reporting-experience-m3b-implementation.md). Business attributes are independently opt-in: `RP_SCENARIO_ATTRIBUTES_ENABLED=true`. The default allowlist is `component,team,owner,layer,priority,browser,tms`. Defaults accept a JSON object/list in `RP_SCENARIO_ATTRIBUTES`; tags use `@key:value`. Feature → Rule → Scenario → executed Examples scopes inherit values; a later scope overrides an earlier one. Conflicts for a key within one scope are ignored for that scope. Attributes apply to Scenario items only. `tms` comes solely from the effective explicit ID, not from independently reselecting inherited tags or configured `tms` defaults. See [attribute usage](../examples/m3c_attributes/README.md) and its [contract](design/reporting-experience-m3c-attributes-implementation.md). Source/CI/TMS links are separately opt-in: `RP_SCENARIO_LINKS_ENABLED=true`. They append bounded validated Markdown links to the existing Scenario description without changing identity, attributes, logs, or test topology. Source requires `{commit}`, `{path}`, `{line}`, a full commit ID, and the source root. CI requires an explicit URL; no provider/environment is autodetected. TMS uses `{id}` from the effective explicit ID rather than the stable hashed wire ID. Invalid references are skipped without logging their raw values. See [link usage](../examples/m3c_links/README.md), [configuration](configuration.md#scenario-identity-and-business-metadata), and the [links contract](design/reporting-experience-m3c-links-implementation.md). ## Video and external storage Recording/finalization, console collection, conversion, privacy, and retention belong to the caller. MP4 multipart attachment does not guarantee inline playback. Ordinary PNG/JSON/text reporting uses default `reportportal_multipart` and needs no external video setup. This guide does not certify MP4 delivery under that mode. Optional `RP_VIDEO_UPLOAD_MODE=minio_markdown` streams caller-finalized video through path-style S3/MinIO and writes video markup plus an **Open video** link. Playback still depends on the RP renderer, browser/codec, CSP, and object access policy. A recording typically becomes complete after BrowserContext close; publish it under the currently open After/manual Hook node, not the failed Step's expired handle.
